chunks: "Mousebites are the little rows of holes you see on the edge of a panelized PCB.
When a board has an irregular outline or gaps between boards, the fab routes the outline but leaves a few narrow tabs holding the board to the panel.

Those tabs would be hard to break cleanly, so instead of leaving them solid, we drill a line of small holes through each tab, usually around half a millimetre in diameter and spaced very close together.
That works like a perforated sheet of paper: when you flex the board, the tab breaks along the line of holes and not wherever it likes.
The name comes from the way the leftover edge looks, like a mouse took little bites out of it.

Design-wise I'd put tabs where there's no copper or components nearby, keep ceramic caps and connectors out of the breakout area, and make sure the stub left on the edge doesn't protrude past the outline the enclosure needs.
If the edge has to be perfectly smooth, I'd ask for a depaneling router or ask the fab to leave the stub recessed into a notch."
